claim: Playa de Somo is an 8+ km dune-backed beach break that runs into Loredo, works at all tides, is beginner-friendly when small and the go-to spot for surf schools in Cantabria.
quote: high quality, consistent beachbreak that can produce well-defined banks that generally work through the tides. With over 8 kms of good beachbreaks it receives good swells coming from all directions all year around

claim: Escuela Cántabra de Surf, one of Europe's best-known surf schools, sits on the Somo beachfront with showers, lockers and parking next to the sand.
quote: Escuela Cántabra de Surf | Escuela de Surf Nº1 en ... - Somo

claim: Playa de Loredo, sheltered from NE winds by Santa Marina island and backed by pine woods and dunes, is regarded as one of Cantabria's best all-round water-sports beaches.
quote: Playa de Loredo en Ribamontán al Mar, Playa con escuela de surf en Cantabria

claim: Ribamontán al Mar was declared Spain's first natural surf reserve (and Europe's second), with Loredo hosting regional championships and Somo selected as the only Spanish venue for the 2026 Rip Curl GromSearch.
quote: 2ª edición del Campeonato de Surf de Loredo

claim: Playa de Langre is a pair of wild golden beaches backed by 25 m cliffs topped with green fields, with surfable waves and access only via a clifftop staircase.
quote: The two gorgeously wild golden beaches of Langre are backed by cliffs topped with rolling green fields, and often have surfable waves.

claim: Langre has minimal parking (around 15 free spaces plus paid overflow at €4/day), strong currents that make casual swimming difficult, and stays uncrowded with 50–100 m of free space around bathers even in season.
quote: public parking for 15 cars and 2 large private cars at 4€ a day

claim: Playa de Galizano (La Canal) is a small, undeveloped natural beach in Ribamontán al Mar popular with local surfers, with free parking that fills quickly in summer.
quote: Galizano / La Canal / La Canal de Galizano Beach - Ribamontán al Mar (Cantabria)

claim: Playa de Berria in Santoña is a 2 km golden-sand crescent between Monte Buciero and Monte El Brusco, backed by dunes and marshland, and one of the region's most reliable beginner-friendly beach breaks.
quote: Berria is a sweeping, 2km-long crescent of golden sand tucked between the headlands of Monte Buciero and Monte El Brusco in Cantabria

claim: Berria sits 2.5 km north of Santoña with frequent €1.55 bus links and a free car park right by the sand, and adjoins the Santoña Marshes nature reserve.
quote: Berria is a sweeping, 2km-long crescent of golden sand tucked between the headlands of Monte Buciero and Monte El Brusco

claim: El Sardinero is Santander's flagship urban beach with lifeguards, a children's play area with summer monitors, sun-lounger and locker hire, mobility lift, and a seafront promenade.
quote: First Beach of El Sardinero | Turismo Santander

claim: Sardinero I has gentle waves suitable for family swimming in the calm waters of the Bay of Biscay, with extensive services and direct city-bus access.
quote: Beach: Sardinero I in Santander. Cantabria | spain.info

claim: The Parque Natural de las Dunas de Liencres covers 1,700 ha at the mouth of the Pas, hosts the best-developed dune complex on the Cantabrian coast, and its main beaches Valdearenas (~2.8 km long) and Canallave combine wild landscape with surf and walking trails.
quote: Parque Natural de las Dunas de Liencres y Costa Quebrada

claim: Playa de Mataleñas is a small (~230 m) sheltered cove on Santander's eastern coast reached by a steep staircase of 156–157 steps, with lifeguards in summer.

Playa de los Locos in Suances lies about 31 km / 26 min west of Santander via A-67 — at the outer edge of a 30 km radius from Villaverde de Pontones — and is a 500 m European Natural Surf Reserve beach with three named peaks for all surf levels.
quote: Surfing at Los Locos Beach, Suances | Complete Guide 2026
